title: Evaluator core (eval/apply)
description: Implement the eval/apply loop over datums. Dispatch on form: self-evaluating, variable reference, special-form lookup, procedure application. Apply handles both primitive and closure procedures. This is the spine; special forms and built-ins plug into it. Tail calls handled by trampolining (proper TCO is a separate later bead but design should leave room).
design:
Evaluator is an explicit step-loop, NOT recursive Rust calls. Shape:

  loop {
      match state {
          Step::Eval(expr, env) => ...,    // -> Step::Apply | Step::Tail | Step::Done
          Step::Apply(proc, args) => ...,  // -> Step::Eval | Step::Done
          Step::Tail(expr, env) => continue, // tail call: no Rust stack growth
          Step::Done(v) => return v,
      }
  }

A continuation is a Vec<Frame> describing pending work. Push a frame when entering a non-tail subexpression; pop when its value is ready. This makes:
  - TCO (T11): free — tail calls reuse the current frame instead of pushing
  - call/cc (T17): clone() the frame vector to capture a continuation; replace the vector to invoke
  - Exception handling (T18): unwind frames searching for a handler

Why: writing eval as recursive Rust calls forces a rewrite for both TCO and call/cc. Bake the shape now; the user-facing call/cc procedure can still ship in T17.

title: Environment and lexical scoping
description: Implement the Environment type: nested frames, lexical lookup, define/set! semantics (define adds to current frame, set! mutates existing binding or errors), shared parent references for closures. Must support efficient lookup and the mutation rules R7RS requires.

title: Core runtime value types
description: Define the Value enum / runtime representation: pair, null, symbol (interned), number (initially fixnum + f64; full tower in later bead), char, string, vector, bytevector, boolean, procedure (primitive + closure), port (stub), eof-object, unspecified. Choose between Rc<RefCell> vs arena vs Gc<T> for cyclic structures — document the choice. Implement eqv?/equal?/eq? semantics.
design:
Cycle handling: use Rc<RefCell<...>> for mutable cells (pairs, vectors, strings, boxes). Document the leak: cyclic structures created via set-car!/set-cdr! will NOT be reclaimed until process exit. This is acceptable for v1 — most amateur Scheme interpreters do this. A proper GC (gc crate or custom mark-sweep) is deferred future work, not in scope for the epic.

Value enum sketch (subject to refinement in implementation):
  Value::Null
  Value::Bool(bool)
  Value::Char(char)
  Value::Symbol(Symbol)            // interned string id
  Value::Int(i64)                  // fast path for fixnums
  Value::BigInt(Rc<BigInt>)        // exact integer overflow
  Value::Rational(Rc<BigRational>) // exact rational
  Value::Float(f64)                // inexact real
  Value::String(Rc<RefCell<String>>)
  Value::Pair(Rc<RefCell<Pair>>)
  Value::Vector(Rc<RefCell<Vec<Value>>>)
  Value::Bytevector(Rc<RefCell<Vec<u8>>>)
  Value::Procedure(Rc<Procedure>)
  Value::Port(Rc<RefCell<Port>>)
  Value::Eof
  Value::Unspecified

Equality:
  eq?: pointer/identity equality for heap values; value equality for atoms
  eqv?: like eq? but with sane number comparison across exact/inexact
  equal?: structural (recurses pairs/vectors/strings)

title: Parser: tokens to datum/AST
description: Build a recursive-descent (or equivalent) parser that turns the token stream into Scheme datums. Handle proper and improper lists, vectors, bytevectors, quote-family reader macros, and produce structured parse errors with source spans. Output is a Datum tree consumable by the evaluator (not a separate IR — Scheme programs are themselves datums).

title: Lexer / tokenizer
description: Tokenize Scheme source text into tokens: identifiers, numbers (with R7RS lexical syntax including #e/#i/#b/#o/#d/#x prefixes), booleans (#t/#f/#true/#false), characters (#\name and #\x...), strings (with escapes), parens, dot, quote/quasiquote/unquote/unquote-splicing reader macros, vector prefix #(, bytevector prefix #u8(, comments (line ;, block #| |#, datum #;). Span/position tracking for error messages.

title: Architecture decision: tree-walking vs bytecode
description: Document the interpreter architecture choice before any evaluator code. Compare tree-walking AST interpreter vs bytecode VM. Recommend tree-walking for v1 (simpler, easier to extend with call/cc and macros). Capture decision and rationale in design notes / bd design field. Output: short ADR-style note committed to the repo.
notes: ADR 0001 written at docs/0001-tree-walking-interpreter.md. Decision: tree-walking iterative evaluator with explicit Step enum and Vec<Frame> continuation stack. Makes TCO free and call/cc a frame-vector clone. Replaces recursive eval. Defers bytecode VM as alternate-backend future work. Created docs/README.md as the index.

title: Cargo project scaffold
description: Initialize the Rust project structure: Cargo.toml (lib + bin crate), src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, basic module layout, lints (clippy/rustfmt config), and a minimal smoke test. No interpreter logic yet — just the skeleton that everything else builds on.
notes:
Scaffold complete:
- Cargo.toml: edition 2024, lib + bin both named 'nscheme', thiserror v2 as the one runtime dep, strict lints (clippy::all + clippy::pedantic warnings, unsafe forbidden, pragmatic allow list).
- src/lib.rs: public surface entry, currently exports just VERSION. Modules added as later beads land.
- src/main.rs: minimal CLI that prints version and a placeholder for the REPL (T10).
- tests/smoke.rs: integration test proving the crate builds and exposes its surface.
- rustfmt.toml: edition 2024, max width 100.
- .gitignore: /target/, beads atomic-write temp files.

Verified: cargo build, cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, cargo run all pass.

Deferred (explicitly NOT in scope for T1):
- CI: no remote yet, so no GitHub Actions / equivalent. Add when a remote exists.
- README.md: per CLAUDE.md, do not create unless requested. docs/ will be populated starting in T2.
close_reason: Scaffold complete; cargo build/test/clippy/fmt all clean.

title: R7RS-small Scheme interpreter in Rust (epic)
description: Implement an R7RS-small conformant Scheme interpreter in Rust. R7RS-small (2013) is the target; R7RS-large libraries (Red/Tangerine dockets, Foundations) may be layered on top as future work. Tracks the full implementation as an epic; individual phases are tracked as dependent beads.

title: R7RS library / module system
description: Implement define-library, import, export, include, include-library-declarations, cond-expand. Support the standard (scheme base), (scheme write), (scheme read), (scheme char), (scheme file), (scheme inexact), (scheme cxr), (scheme lazy), (scheme load), (scheme process-context), (scheme repl), (scheme time), (scheme case-lambda), (scheme eval), (scheme r5rs) library names — at least stubs that re-export from the implementation.

title: syntax-rules macros
description: Implement R7RS hygienic macros via syntax-rules: define-syntax let-syntax letrec-syntax, pattern matching with literals and ..., template expansion with hygiene (alpha-renaming of introduced identifiers). syntax-rules is the only macro system required by R7RS-small. syntax-case is NOT required and deferred.

title: I/O and ports
description: R7RS port system: input-port? output-port? textual-port? binary-port?, current-input-port current-output-port current-error-port, open-input-file open-output-file open-input-string open-output-string get-output-string, read read-char peek-char read-line read-string eof-object? eof-object, write display newline write-char write-string, close-port close-input-port close-output-port, with-input-from-file with-output-to-file, file-exists? delete-file.

title: Strings, chars, symbols, vectors, bytevectors
description: Full R7RS-small ops for these data types: string-length string-ref substring string-append string->list list->string string-copy string-copy! string-fill! string=? string<? etc.; char->integer integer->char char-alphabetic? etc.; symbol->string string->symbol; make-vector vector-length vector-ref vector-set! vector->list list->vector vector-copy vector-copy! vector-fill!; bytevector ops (make-bytevector bytevector-u8-ref/set! bytevector-copy bytevector-append utf8->string string->utf8).

title: Numeric tower
description: Full R7RS numeric tower: exact integers (arbitrary precision via num-bigint or similar), exact rationals, inexact reals (f64), exact/inexact conversions, exact->inexact, inexact->exact, number->string with radix, string->number, integer? rational? real? complex? number?, exact? inexact?. Complex numbers optional (mark as deferred if not needed).

title: Tail call optimization
description: Implement proper tail-call handling per R7RS section 3.5. Use a trampoline / explicit eval loop so tail positions don't consume stack. Verify with deep recursion tests (e.g., (define (loop n) (if (= n 0) 'done (loop (- n 1)))) with n=1_000_000).
notes: Architecture for TCO is decided in T7's design field (eval is an explicit step-loop with continuation frames). This bead is the 'surface' work: verify deep recursion (1M-deep self-call doesn't overflow), audit each special form to ensure it correctly distinguishes tail vs non-tail positions, write conformance tests covering R7RS section 3.5 tail positions.

title: REPL
description: Interactive read-eval-print loop. Read a complete datum (handle multi-line input by counting parens), evaluate in a persistent top-level env, print the result. Use rustyline or similar for line editing and history. Bound to the bin crate (cargo run launches REPL).

title: Built-in procedures (base library subset)
description: Implement (scheme base) procedures: arithmetic (+ - * / quotient remainder modulo abs min max), comparison (= < > <= >=), predicates (null? pair? number? symbol? procedure? boolean? string? vector? char? eof-object? etc.), equality (eq? eqv? equal?), list ops (car cdr cons list length append reverse map for-each list-ref member assoc), boolean (not). Numeric tower depth is limited here — full tower comes in a later bead.

title: Core special forms
description: Implement R7RS-small special forms: quote, if, lambda, define, set!, begin, let, let*, letrec, letrec*, let-values, let*-values, cond (with => clauses), case, and, or, when, unless, do, delay, parameterize, quasiquote/unquote/unquote-splicing. Derived forms can be expressed in terms of core forms; document which are primitive vs derived.

title: R7RS conformance test suite
description: Wire up an existing R7RS-small conformance test suite (e.g., chibi-scheme's test suite, or write our own derived from the spec) as cargo test-integration. Track which sections pass/fail. Used as the acceptance gate for the epic.

title: Exception handling
description: R7RS exception system: raise raise-continuable with-exception-handler, guard form, error error-object? error-object-message error-object-irritants error-object-message read-error? file-error?. Integrate with dynamic-wind from the continuations bead.

title: call/cc and continuations
description: Implement first-class continuations: call-with-current-continuation (call/cc), dynamic-wind. R7RS requires full one-shot AND multi-shot continuations. Common approaches: CPS transform of the evaluator, or capture-the-stack via Rust generators / explicit continuation objects. Choose and document the approach. Verify with classic call/cc tests (generator patterns, escape continuations, coroutines).
notes: Architecture for call/cc is decided in T7's design field (continuation = Vec<Frame>, cloning captures, replacing invokes). This bead is the surface work: expose call-with-current-continuation, dynamic-wind, the continuation procedure value type, and the before/after thunk semantics.
